definitions.explanation: Waste materials that cannot be incinerated, such as glass, ceramics, and metals. In Japanese garbage sorting, this is one of the main categories alongside burnable waste and recyclables.

examples.japanese: {不燃物|ふねんぶつ}は{水曜日|すいようび}に{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Non-burnable waste is put out on Wednesdays.

examples.japanese: ガラスや{陶器|とうき}は{不燃物|ふねんぶつ}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: Glass and ceramics are classified as non-burnable waste.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しで{出|で}た{不燃物|ふねんぶつ}をまとめて{処分|しょぶん}した。
examples.english: I disposed of all the non-burnable waste that came out from moving.

notes:
Compound of {不燃|ふねん} (non-combustible) + {物|ぶつ} (thing/material).

EXAMPLES OF {不燃物|ふねんぶつ}:
- ガラス (glass)
- {陶器|とうき} (ceramics)
- {金属|きんぞく} (metals)
- {小型|こがた}{家電|かでん} (small appliances)

CONTRAST:
- {可燃物|かねんぶつ}/{燃|も}えるゴミ: burnable waste (opposite)
- {資源|しげん}ゴミ: recyclable waste
- {粗大|そだい}ゴミ: oversized waste

ALSO CALLED:
{不燃|ふねん}ゴミ or {燃|も}えないゴミ in everyday language.

CULTURE:
Japanese municipalities have strict garbage sorting rules. {不燃物|ふねんぶつ} collection days vary by area and are typically less frequent than burnable waste days.
